blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 5 killings of trans and gender-identity-diverse people in 2025, placing it in the mid-band alongside two sibling states/provinces. Against a population of about 7.2 million the rate is approximately 0.69 per million per year, about 1.8 times the national rate of 0.38 per million. This state/province sits on an agricultural-frontier savanna belt, and the national dossier notes that 68% of 2024 killings occurred outside state/provincial capitals - in interior towns where a visitor's exposure may be harder to mitigate.

The rate and the absence of any mitigating legal or institutional finding place this state/province modestly below the national norm. Against the neighbouring mining state, which had 8 killings in 2025, the lower absolute count of this state/province partly reflects a smaller population, but the per-capita gap (0.69 versus the national 0.38 per million) is directionally consistent with a moderate below-average penalty. No unit-specific ordinance or statutory restriction was identified.
